title: 168 referring domains (17% of the profile) point at URLs that 301 into hub index pages - the soft-404 trap, dominated by 69 dead blog posts funnelled to /blog

evidence.claim: 168 of 995 distinct referring domains in the live backlink export link to a URL whose crawl finalUrl is a hub index (/blog, /technology, /, /contact, etc.); 142 of them with at least one dofollow link
evidence.source: ahrefs/backlinks.export.json (12,795 rows) joined to crawl/urls.json finalUrl
evidence.value: 168/995 domains; /blog receives 154 domains via 69 dead blog URLs (359 links); /technology's 2,929 links are only 4 scraper domains

evidence.claim: None of the 69 dead blog URLs has a live article with the same slug - every apparent slug match is itself a catch-all redirect (hopCount>0), so no exact-match redirect target exists in the current content set
evidence.source: crawl/urls.json (status==200 AND hopCount==0 filter) vs the 69 dead paths

evidence.claim: Verified live: legacy blog paths 301 to the /blog hub, which Google treats as a soft 404 for link-equity purposes

effort.note: mapping is mechanical; per-URL target choice needs a human eye for topical relevance

impact.estimate: 154 referring domains' worth of equity currently evaporating into /blog. The top ~15 dead URLs carry 30/20/14/11/10 refdomains each with top source DR 76-94. Re-pointing each to the closest topically-relevant live article (e.g. why-philippines-for-business -> /hiring-tips/hiring-developers-in-the-philippines-...; 5-challenges-hiring -> /blog/it-outsourcing/the-5-challenges... is dead, use /hiring-tips equivalents) recovers equity a DR 36 site cannot afford to waste.

recommendation: Rank the 69 dead blog URLs by referring domains (list computed, in authority.md). For each of the top ~25, pick the closest topically-relevant LIVE article and add a specific 301; where none exists (lifestyle content: eating-healthy-at-work, sci-fi-movies), leave the hub redirect and accept the loss explicitly. Do NOT blanket-redirect all 69 - an irrelevant 301 is a soft 404 and wastes the link anyway.

title: 46% of all live backlinks reach the site only through cloudemployee.co.uk 301 redirect chains - the legacy domain is load-bearing for half the link profile

evidence.claim: 5,864 of 12,795 live backlinks have cloudemployee.co.uk in their redirect chain; a further 702 route via other redirects; only 6,229 point directly at cloudemployee.io
The top external anchor by referring domains is the legacy domain itself
Ahrefs corroborates at profile level: 5,586 of 8,913 backlinks are flagged as redirect-type

impact.estimate: If the .co.uk registration or its redirect config ever lapses, ~46% of the live link profile disappears at once. Also: many .co.uk deep links chain .co.uk -> www path -> hub (double hop ending in a soft 404), compounding AUTH-01.

recommendation: Confirm cloudemployee.co.uk registration is on auto-renew with long expiry and that its redirect map is documented and monitored (a simple uptime check on 2-3 known .co.uk URLs). Treat the domain as permanent SEO infrastructure, never a candidate for cost-cutting. Where the biggest .co.uk-sourced links chain into hub catch-alls, fix at the www side via AUTH-01 targets.

title: The /alternatives hub links to only 15 of 30 compare pages; the other 15 - including the site's top Google page and top Copilot-cited pages - have zero or one internal inlink

evidence.claim: /compare/toptal-vs-upwork has 0 internal inlinks and is the site's biggest impression earner outside home
evidence.source: joined/pages.json (clean URL row, query-param variants excluded) + crawl/internal-links.json (0 linkers)

evidence.claim: Verified live 8 Aug: /alternatives page 1 renders links to exactly 15 /compare/ detail pages; the rest sit only behind ?page=2 pagination

The most-AI-cited pages are among the unlinked: /compare/dedicated-teams-vs-toptal (2,351 Copilot citations, 27% of all) has 1 inlink; /compare/cloud-employee-vs-proxify (674 citations) and /compare/cloud-employee-vs-upwork (278) have 0
Distribution across the 684 real pages with inlink data: 94 have zero inlinks, 198 have exactly one
evidence.source: joined/pages.json internal_links_in (note: some zero rows are query-param URL variants; the counts above were spot-checked on clean URLs)
evidence.value: 0 inlinks: 94 rows; 1 inlink: 198 rows; 43 of the single-inlink pages earn impressions or hold backlinks

impact.estimate: /compare/toptal-vs-upwork alone: 44,019 impressions at position 7 with ~0.03% CTR; compare pages at pos 7-11 with zero internal equity are the cheapest ranking improvement available. Moving the pos 8-11 cluster (vs-fiverr, vs-contra, vs-upwork, ~3,800 combined impressions) into the top 5 is plausibly tens of extra clicks/month on buying-intent queries, and these same pages drive 45% of AI citations.

recommendation: Make every compare page reachable from page 1: raise the /alternatives first-page card count to 30, or add a compact 'All comparisons' text-link block on the hub, in the footer of each compare page (related-comparisons module), and cross-link compare pages from the topically matching service pages. Same pattern for the 43 single-inlink pages with impressions (list in authority.md - mostly /services/* and /technology/* detail pages at 1,200-3,700 impressions each).

title: DR 36 vs 70-90 for every competitor, but backlink quantity is not the binding constraint the raw numbers suggest - keyword footprint is

evidence.claim: Head-to-head: Cloud Employee DR 36 / 692 refdomains / 48 US keywords / 415 organic traffic vs Toptal DR 90 / 47,172 rd / 17,670 kw / 194,785 traffic; Turing DR 74 / 8,357 rd / 2,511 kw; arc.dev DR 72 / 5,003 rd / 4,895 kw; Andela DR 71 / 5,406 rd / 49 kw / 2,339 traffic; Revelo DR 70 / 4,158 rd / 395 kw

Andela holds 5,406 refdomains (7.8x ours) yet ranks for only 49 US keywords (we rank for 48) - authority without content footprint buys little; arc.dev converts similar authority into 4,895 keywords via content
evidence.value: Andela 49 kw vs arc.dev 4,895 kw at comparable DR

impact.estimate: Strategic framing for the roadmap: link outreach (AUTH-05) matters, but the Andela-vs-arc.dev contrast in the same dataset shows content footprint is the multiplier on whatever authority exists. Ranking 48 keywords at DR 36 with 16 in the top 3 says the domain can rank when a page targets a keyword.

recommendation: Use this as the prioritisation frame at synthesis: content-gap-driven page creation (content lens territory) compounds faster than outreach at this DR. Outreach and content are not either/or, but if forced to sequence, content first.

evidence.claim: 28 broken-backlink rows (24 distinct after dedupe), sorted by source DR: 91, 75, 73, 61, 59, 58, 55, 53, 53, 48...; 6 papasearch.net rows are a DR 18 scraper and worthless
The DR 91 target /blog/tech-news/the-future-of-drone-technology%20 404s only because of the trailing space; the unspaced path already 308s (into the /blog catch-all)
No live article shares a slug with any of the dead URLs, so every redirect is a topical-nearest-match judgment, not a mechanical mapping
evidence.source: crawl/urls.json live-page slug index vs dead paths

impact.estimate: Honest read: smaller than the headline DRs suggest. The DR 91 source is a myportfolio.com citations page (UR 0, traffic 0); the real wins are DR 75 testgorilla.com (56k traffic domain, dofollow, anchor 'some key features' on an NDA article) and DR 61 economicsonline.co.uk. /team/shawnee-malesich carries 286 citations (3.3%, 9th most-cited page) and returns 404 in production

title: Copilot collapse (26-27 Jul): no corroborating signal anywhere in GSC - Google impressions ROSE 36% the same week; Bing-side index event, cause unknown, watch weekly

evidence.claim: Copilot: 186 citations/10 pages on 26 Jul -> 58/4 on 27 Jul -> 13/2 on 28 Jul -> 0/0 on 2 Aug; recovery since cutover: 9, 13, 23
evidence.value: cited PAGES collapsed 10->2, i.e. pages fell out of the grounding set, not a per-page citation decay

evidence.claim: GSC daily impressions over the same boundary: mean 4,120/day (12-26 Jul) vs 5,592/day (27 Jul-2 Aug), +36%; clicks and position flat
evidence.value: no negative Google-side signal at all

impact.estimate: Confirms the migration is exonerated (started a week before cutover) AND the site is exonerated (Google went up while Copilot went down). Cause is on Bing's side - index refresh, grounding-set change, or the Webflow site's crawl state pre-cutover. The correct posture is watch, not fix.

recommendation: No action beyond monitoring. Track the AIPerformanceOverviewStats weekly; if cited pages have not recovered to ~10/day by end of August, the post-cutover Bing recrawl did not restore the grounding set and a Bing Webmaster investigation (IndexNow, sitemap ping) becomes worthwhile. Note 3 of the top-10 recovering citations now land on the new Next.js pages, so the recovery is happening against OUR site.

title: Internal anchor text is healthy overall (only ~3% generic), but Material icon ligature names are leaking into anchors and 2,046 blog-card links say 'read full story'

evidence.claim: Of 38,605 internal anchors: 650 empty, 1,130 generic ('view all' 684, 'read article' 442, 'here' 4), 2,046 'read full story' blog-card CTAs; everything else is descriptive nav/footer/contextual text
evidence.value: ~9.9% generic-or-empty including 'read full story'; ~4.6% excluding it

evidence.claim: Icon ligature text is concatenated into anchor strings sitewide: 'location_oneastern europetop-tier technical and ai talent', 'event_upcomingevents & webinars', 'calculatetools & quizzes', 'downloadfree downloads' - 686 occurrences each (every page's chrome)
evidence.value: Material Symbols ligature names crawled as anchor text

impact.estimate: Minor relevance noise: crawlers read 'location_oneastern europe...' as link text on every page. The blog-card fix ('read full story' -> the article title, or aria-label the card) is the standard pattern and touches 2,046 links in one component.

recommendation: Two component-level fixes: (1) hide icon glyphs from the accessibility/text tree (aria-hidden on the icon span) so anchors read clean; (2) make the blog-card CTA carry the article title. Neither needs design. Cross-lens: this is also an a11y finding.

title: External anchor profile is 75% brand/URL - clean but zero money-keyword signal - and carries a visible link-spam footprint from an 'SEOExpress' vendor targeting cloudemployee domains

evidence.claim: Brand-or-URL anchors = 1,009 of 1,346 refdomain-anchor pairs (75%): 'cloudemployee.co.uk' 284, 'cloudemployee' 164, 'cloudemployee.io' 108, 'Cloud Employee' 45
evidence.value: healthy, penalty-safe, but no descriptive-anchor equity for target keywords

evidence.claim: ~80+ refdomains carry spam anchors of the form 'Strengthen cloudemployee.io through contextual backlinks, premium guest posts...' and 'A friend told me about SEOExpress.org when cloudemployee.com.au was...' - all nofollow, referencing cloudemployee.com.au and .io

impact.estimate: The spam is nofollow and currently inert - no action forced, but worth knowing it exists before anyone reads raw refdomain counts as 987 'real' domains (the true clean count is lower). The 75% brand share means the outreach in AUTH-05 should aim for descriptive anchors where editorially natural.

recommendation: No disavow (nofollow spam does not need one and disavowing is riskier than ignoring). Flag: is cloudemployee.com.au a domain CE owns or a squatter? The spam cluster targets it alongside .io. Ask Seb; if it is not CE's, ignore entirely.
